rules.sentence: Balloon angioplastyhas been done, especially in critically ill infants, but surgical repair of the coarctation is most commonly performed.
Ballooning and stenting of older patients with coarctation has become more accepted as primary therapy, but surgical repair remains a common form of management.

Cyanotic congenital heart disease occurs when some of the systemic venous return crosses from the right side of the heart to the left and returns to the body without going through the lungs (righttoleft shunt).
Cyanosis, the visible sign of this shunt, occurs when approximately 5 g/100 mL of reduced hemoglobin is present in systemic blood.
Thus, a polycythemic patient appears cyanotic with a lower percentage of reduced hemoglobin.
A patient with anemia requires a higher percentage of reduced hemoglobin for the recognition of cyanosis.
The most common cyanotic congenital heart defects are the five Ts: Tetralogy of FallotTransposition of the great arteriesTricuspid atresiaTruncus arteriosus Total anomalous pulmonary venous return
